entries.0d410d6a0ec10abc: With the corporate philosophy "As a logistics company centered on the shipping industry, we contribute to people's enriched lives," its basic policy is to increase corporate value while promoting low-carbon and decarbonization for itself and society. In its 5-year medium-term management plan from fiscal 2022 to fiscal 2026 (announced May 9, 2022), it allocates management resources by dividing roles by business. Businesses in the role of driving growth are iron ore and steel raw materials, car carriers, and LNG carriers; businesses in the role of supporting the energy transition and taking on new business opportunities are thermal coal, oil tankers, and LPG carriers; and businesses in the role of contributing by polishing their earning power are bulk carriers, coastal and domestic shipping, and ports and logistics. It positions the container ship business as being in the role of supporting, as a shareholder, the growth of ONE, an equity-method affiliate, and also aims to expand new business areas such as liquefied CO2 transportation and offshore wind power support vessels.

entries.5263103c4688ec0f: This business handles cargo handling and warehousing at ports, towage, arrangement of international cargo transport, and logistics for finished vehicles. For the fiscal year ended March 2026, container terminal handling volume in the domestic logistics and port business, the number of towage jobs in the towage business and warehousing volume in the warehousing business were each firm. In the international logistics business, some cargo movements, mainly automobile-related cargo in the air transport of the forwarding business, were sluggish, while semiconductor transport volume increased. In the finished vehicle logistics business, new vehicle sales, which affect handling volumes at ports in Australia, were at the same level as the previous year, and transport and storage volumes remained generally stable. Main consolidated subsidiaries in this business include Daitō Corporation, Nitō Butsuryū Co., Ltd. and Shīgēto Corporation, which are port transport businesses; Nitō Tagu Co., Ltd., a towage business; K Line Logistics Ltd., an air freight agency business; and Nihon Kōsoku Yusō Co., Ltd., a trucking business (as of March 31, 2026). entries.6f790ddb46057262: Dry Bulk transports iron ore, bauxite, coal and other cargo using large and medium and small ships. Energy Resources operates LNG carriers, LPG carriers, electric-power coal carriers, large crude oil tankers, drillships (offshore drilling vessels) and FPSOs (floating production, storage and offloading units) under medium- to long-term charter contracts. Product Logistics consists of the automobile carrier business, which transports automobiles on car carriers; logistics businesses such as port cargo handling, warehousing, tugboat services and arrangement of international cargo transport (forwarding); the coastal and domestic cargo shipping business (including ferries); and the container shipping business. It is also engaged in businesses aimed at decarbonization, such as the liquefied CO2 carrier 'NORTHERN PIONEER' (completed November 2024) and offshore work support vessel business related to offshore wind power generation.
entries.6fb62933322e6401: This is a segment consisting solely of the dry bulk business, transporting cargo such as iron ore, bauxite and coal on large vessels and on mid-sized and small vessels. For the fiscal year ended March 2026, revenue from external customers was ¥292,783 million (28.8% of group revenue, down 9.2% year on year), making it the 2nd-largest business among the reportable segments. Large vessel market conditions remained generally firm against a backdrop of firm demand for iron ore and bauxite, while mid-sized and small vessel market conditions softened at times in the first half due to weak demand for coal transport, but recovered from early 2026 and remained firm. Main constituent companies are Kawasaki Kisen Kaisha, Ltd., K LINE BULK SHIPPING (UK) LIMITED, K LINE PTE LTD and K Line (India) Shipping Private Limited (as of March 31, 2026).

entries.88ace6ddff4c46b1: This segment consists of the coastal business and the domestic business, which comprises ferry, scheduled liner and tramp shipping services. For the fiscal year ended March 2026, in the coastal business, steel volume declined year on year, while biomass fuel and bulk cargo increased, and overall transport volume exceeded the previous year's level. In the domestic business, ferry transport increased for trucks, passenger cars and passengers alike, with passenger cars and passengers performing particularly strongly. Scheduled liner transport was firm on the Tomakomai route, but overall volume fell below the previous year due to factors including rough weather and poor crop harvests. In tramp shipping, transport of limestone declined, while coal transport and general cargo ships were firm. Kawasaki Kinkai Kisen Co., Ltd., which is involved in this business, was established in May 1966 by separating the company's domestic division and became a wholly owned subsidiary through a share exchange in June 2022. Revenue for this segment is not presented separately.

entries.dd08b58740a48bb3: The group is centered on Kawasaki Kisen Kaisha, Ltd. (the filing company) and comprises domestic and overseas consolidated subsidiaries and companies accounted for by the equity method. The business consists of three reportable [[term:segment|segments]], Dry Bulk, Energy Resources and Product Logistics, and 'Other,' which is not included in the reportable segments. Container shipping is not carried out by a consolidated subsidiary; it is undertaken by OCEAN NETWORK EXPRESS PTE. LTD. (ONE) and its holding company Ocean Network Express Holdings Ltd., and the latter is an [[term:equity-method|equity-method]] affiliate in which 31.0% of the voting rights are held (as of March 31, 2026). The consolidated subsidiaries labeled 'other 176 companies' include 176 vessel-owning subsidiaries located in flag-of-convenience countries. The number of employees is 5,262 (fiscal year ended March 2026).

entries.fc8c891ddcc6ca99: This business transports automobiles using car carriers. The history section records the combined bulk and car carrier Dai-ichi Toyota Maru (completed November 1968), Japan's first car carrier, named PURE CAR CARRIER (PCC), Dai-jū Toyota Maru (completed July 1970), the next-generation environmentally friendly car carrier DRIVE GREEN HIGHWAY (completed February 2016), and the next-generation environmentally friendly LNG-fueled car carrier CENTURY HIGHWAY GREEN (completed March 2021). For the fiscal year ended March 2026, car sales in each country were generally firm overall, while the impact of additional U.S. tariffs and the deterioration of the Middle East situation at period-end led to changes in vessel deployment and higher operating costs such as fuel. Revenue for this segment is not presented separately.
